quote: Great. This is Corey with Ion. I, gotten a request here you're looking at solar for your home. Is that right?
stewart_read: The customer's later comments confirm this is a Tesla-sourced lead ('the ad I responded to said that Tesla was looking for people'), but the rep opens with the generic standard-lead intro rather than the Tesla-certified-installer framing. He never attempted the Tesla variant at all — this isn't a degraded execution of it, it's a missed selection of the correct intro for this lead source.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may not have had visibility into the lead source before dialing, making the generic intro a data problem rather than a rep-skill problem.
coaching_implication: Confirm whether lead-source tagging is visible to setters before the call. If it is, coach Corey to check lead source and select the matching intro variant — the Tesla framing directly pre-empts the objection that ultimately killed this call.

quote: The ad kinda inferred that there was no cost involved.
stewart_read: This is the customer naming, almost verbatim, the exact expectation-gap risk the schema flags for a subset of Tesla-sourced leads. It surfaces in the first 40 seconds, well before the rep has any qualification info, and signals the legitimacy conversation isn't finished yet.
coaching_implication: This is the earliest point the rep could have deployed the schema's clean reframe (Tesla referred the lead; Ion sells its own panels plus Powerwall). Instead the rep answered only the cost half of the question, leaving the brand/product half open to resurface later.

quote: Well, you'll be happy to hear that with our program for the bill swap that I mentioned earlier, you just need to have a credit score above 650 to qualify for that. Is that the case, Story?
stewart_read: The rep states a 650 credit threshold, but the schema's documented qualifier is 670. This is the same drift pattern already flagged once in the corpus (SESSION18_fcbf33c1), suggesting either an outdated number circulating among reps or genuine confusion about current policy.
alternative_hypothesis: Policy may have changed to 650 and the schema's 670 is stale — this needs Kenny's reconciliation, not an assumption the rep is wrong.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny: two independent reps have now stated 650 against a schema value of 670. This needs a floor-wide policy confirmation, not a one-off correction to this rep.

quote: Well, you know, it varies greatly. It was almost, like, it was, like, $3.84 last month.
stewart_read: Rep captures the bill figure and reacts ('Oh, jeez. I can definitely see why you're looking into this') but never flips it into alignment-against-the-utility language or ties it forward to the appointment — he moves straight into the credit qualifier.
coaching_implication: Coach Corey to use the acknowledgment as a bridge line — e.g., naming that the design team will show him what that number becomes as a solar payment instead — rather than pivoting immediately to the next verify item.

quote: Unfortunately, not. So those have been back ordered for the better half of this decade.
stewart_read: When the customer directly asks whether the product is the Tesla shingle he saw advertised, the rep confirms it isn't available but frames it as a supply/back-order problem rather than clarifying the actual Ion/Tesla relationship (lead-source referral, Ion's own panels, Powerwall option). This answer is honest but leaves the customer's core misunderstanding about what company/product he's dealing with completely unaddressed.
coaching_implication: This is the single moment that ends the call. Coach Corey on the schema's exact reframe language for this scenario so the next Tesla-ad-sourced customer gets a credibility-building answer instead of a vague supply excuse.

quote: In that case, I'm probably not interested.
stewart_read: This isn't the scripted 'changed my mind' objection Ion has a canonical curiosity-creation response for — it's the customer walking away from a genuine unmet expectation. The rep does not attempt any curiosity-creation move or clarifying question before accepting the exit.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer's disappointment is about product identity, not price or savings, a curiosity-creation pivot ('most people still find real value in what we actually offer') may not have saved this specific call — the mismatch was structural, not emotional.
coaching_implication: Even if this exact call was unlikely to be saved, coach the instinct to ask one clarifying/curiosity question before letting go, rather than immediately accepting the exit with 'No problem, Greg.'

quote: No problem, Greg. Well, appreciate your time, and hope you have a good one. Alright. Thanks.
stewart_read: The call ends with no next step, no attempt to re-anchor to what Ion actually offers, and no path back to the lead — a clean but total loss with zero salvage attempt.
coaching_implication: Even on a lost call, coach a lightweight parting line that keeps the door open (e.g., offering to follow up with accurate product info) rather than a full, final goodbye.
